claims.text: Large language models excel at numerical estimation.
Large language models struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty.
Large language models are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers.
Nominal 99% confidence intervals constructed by LLMs cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average across several modern models.
A conformal prediction based approach that adjusts confidence intervals obtains accurate 99% observed coverage for LLM answers.
A conformal prediction based approach decreases the Winkler interval score by 54%.
Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment methods reduce LLM overconfidence at high confidence levels.
When reasoning under uncertainty, LLMs act as if sampling from a truncated region of their inferred distribution, neglecting its tails.

evidence.description: Across several modern models, nominal 99% intervals cover the true answer only 65% of the time on average.
With a conformal prediction based approach that adjusts the intervals... the Winkler interval score decreases by 54%.

methodologies.name: FermiEval
methodologies.description: A benchmark of Fermi-style estimation questions equipped with a scoring rule for confidence interval coverage and sharpness.

methodologies.name: Conformal prediction interval adjustment
methodologies.description: An approach that adjusts LLM-generated confidence intervals to achieve calibrated observed coverage.

methodologies.name: Direct log-probability elicitation and quantile adjustment
methodologies.description: Methods that elicit direct log-probabilities and adjust quantiles to mitigate overconfidence at high confidence levels.

methodologies.name: Perception-tunnel theory
methodologies.description: A theoretical framework explaining overconfidence by modeling reasoning under uncertainty as sampling from a truncated inferred distribution.

limitations.text: LLMs struggle to correctly quantify uncertainty and are systematically overconfident when constructing confidence intervals around their own answers.
